1777:
Dear Tabula,
I still don’t know where you disappeared off to and it is unlikely that you will ever read this, but it has been a year since we arrived in Empire City. So much has happened this past year. Between winning a war and completely re-assembling the Lamplighters in Kingsbridge, I haven’t had much time to myself! I couldn’t be more thankful for that fact.


1781:
Dear Tabula,
It has been a while. I feel like I should write you again, though I won’t send the letter. The Lamplighters have grown, and as of last few months, are now connected to all states in Arcania. This has meant a lot of travelling for me. I have been to Maine and Georgia and every state in between at this point. Maine was particularly interesting, as Eliza, Julie, Bowen, and I were nearly swallowed by a sentient fog. Thankfully, the fog could speak Common and we were able to de-escalate.

1784:
Dear Tabula,
The strangest thing has happened to me. I write to you now from my bedroom, with my husband (my husband!) asleep next to me. It is quite early in the morning, but I was hardly able to sleep after yesterday’s festivities. It was beautiful. Vivica, Finn, and Eliza truly never hold back, and I am eternally grateful to them. It was strange to get married, without anyone from my time before Empire City, but I could hardly expect my mother to show up (though I did, with Bowen’s help, send a message her way to no reply), or you, wherever you may be. Tomorrow, Bowen and I leave for the Carolinas for a well-earned vacation. I have heard that the waves are a good temperature and in the sand there are the most marvellous shells. I look forward to the calmness of the waters.

1791:
Tabula,
I have not been this exhausted since ‘76, and I am a full 15 years older now. The Whiskey Rebellion has finally ceased, and I can report to Finn and the rest of the Triumvirate tomorrow. I heard a name, as well, someone who had been arming the rebellion with oddly advanced weapons…. A man by the name of Ebuc. I will be sure to talk with Record Keeper once I can return to the office. Speaking of the office, the building recently added two new stories. I think the building just *might* be telling me something about our numbers.

1811:
Dear Tabula,
I am moving West. I have, at this point, given up any hope of seeing you again. I hope that you are all right, wherever you are. I have officially retired from the Lamplighters, and the title of Director has been passed on to someone I could not approve of more. Bowen and Finn have not stopped talking about the West, about the hub of media that it could become. This is all fine and well, but as my husband becomes a famous moving pictures star, I hope he won’t forget about me, and the cottage he promised we could build together. I will be leaving this journal in the Home Office. I have a feeling someone will find it one day.

Epilogue ~Roy and Sabrine~
***Part 1: Empire City Before the Journey West***, as told to Gil, Warden of Waters

'Morning, Gil. How's things holding up for you? We've been setting up shelters for as many people displaced from Hampstead as we can. Most of them in the borough itself, but also some free of iron and silver in the park for people waiting on medical care. I've mostly been caring for people rather than physical work, but Kukudh's barely had a chance to rest with all the messages and deliveries - not that they'd admit they're tired. So whenever I can get a moment between making berries, stabilising people, just talking to people who need it - I've been helping them with heavier deliveries.'

'I ended up at Ferrytown one morning to pick up some enchanted blankets, but I got there a bit too early, so decided to sit under a tree and wait. Next thing I knew it was afternoon, one of the blankets was covering me, and the rest were in a box nearby. It was... heavier than I expected, but I managed to carry it back. Turns out - someone had put a lot of other supplies in with the blankets, with a note saying they were for the people of Hampstead. I don't know who it was, but they have our thanks.'

'Even once the rebuilding is complete, I'm hoping we can continue providing food and shelter for people who need it. With the two of us, we at least have some variety in berries if there's nothing else, and by the time we leave, we should have people able to help.'

"Hey, Gil. Hope you're doing well. Today we finished helping Secel and Jean-Paul with their house over in Hampstead. Good thing we started with some rudimentary cleanup of the borough and set up some huts and other shelters to the survivors first. Some of the people were there back when we were putting the money changer's place back up, and it seems that they remembered it. There is a spark of hope. People started helping one another. Some even offered to help us with Secel's and Jean-Paul's place."

Roy sighs.
"I was worried about it - after all, building a house for a few while the rest are getting temporary huts. But, looks like people decided that the place where their close ones rest needs caretakers. Anyway, the park will have new, trusted caretakers while we're traveling - Fuddles and Cairn decided to move here. I know the park will be in good hands. And it'll be fitting for the house for her family to be built upon the cornerstone she inscribed. We're starting drawing plans in a few days, we have some other things to do in the meantime.."

'Gil, I finally found an opportunity to go to the library... I know, you said it would be better to move on, and I agree - but I'd rather have made one last look for answers, so I can move forwards without the guilt of not trying to apologise. I looked into news, genealogy records, obituaries, and I found... not much. But enough that I know there's little point in searching further.'

'Lovlatar, first. Soon after I died, a lady named Crescens Lovlatar was found dead nearby. It ended up as a cold case, as she seemed to have no external injuries, and no valuables were taken from her besides a--- besides my hat and dress. With that, and that I could take her name... I doubt it was natural causes, as that would imply I had been travelling with her to know it. So my conclusion is that either the ***Thing*** killed her, or I did... All I can do now, though, is pray she's resting peacefully - it would likely cause more problems than it would solve to let people know...'

'As for Louhi. I... found my own obituary. Pretty strange thing to read, all things considered. I - and others - died to a British airship attack, which the news claims came from Hampstead. Although their only proof was me - I was being prepared for burial when I woke up. The Redcoat I remember throwing me out was one who just happened to be stationed there, who was worried about Hampstead's fog creeping into the village. Which I can understand.'
'I'm not going to look into it any more. I've done all I can, without digging too deep... at least, here. I'm... still thinking about the, ah, other thing...'

"Mornin', Gil. The plan's progressing nicely. Not only several people, probably more than necessary, donated their airships for the cause. Based on the prototype I built out of the Aphid, we definitely have enough resources."

"Oh yeah, Jigsaw's helping improve upon the initial design, using all the stuff they had in the workshop where Mal had his tank built. We got some folks from the old Blackthumb guild on it too. The prototype is already running, though on low gear, but I'll probably take it down in a few days to improve it. At least Edriata's happy with the initial findings."

'...alright, Gil. I made my decision. I'm... not going to try bringing back Katrine with the emergency resurrection you left us. As much as I want to... it wouldn't be fair to her, for a start. It's been so long, she's probably moved on - I wouldn't want to risk causing her pain by, as Kukudh puts it---'
`Yoinking her back into this material plane.`
'That, yes. Thanks, Kukudh. A-anyway. With how little I can remember, I doubt anything would be guaranteed to work without... a lot more research, that would throw me back into the past again. And trying with what I know now, and failing, would do the same thing. No - all I can do is live, and honour her memory. And who knows... perhaps she'll find her way to you somehow. If she does - please look after her as you did for me.'

"Hey, Gil. We've done it. Along the east side of the Hudson there's now about a dozen fully-functioning water-purifying stations. They should only need maintenance every once in a while, to replenish essence fuel, and replace the filters with clean ones. By our predictions, with the west side protected by Feytown's magic, it should take between a few months and a year to be absolutely sure we can consider the river clean. The magic others have provided will speed up the initial cleanup, but the stations will then be able to run in the future, and make sure the river stays that way."

"I hope that helps you as much as it'll help the city. I'll need to find people who'll keep the stations going while we're away. I have a few ideas already. Now I'm just thinking what I can do with all the spare parts. Don't worry, I'll figure something out. I'm not leaving any mess behind."

"Hi Gil. It's been a week or two since we last were here in the park. Our trip to the other states was pretty eventful. I thought we could still use the opportunity as sort of a test run of our road trip. The other states haven't been hit as much by the war as the City, and looks like despite their allegiance to the Union, many people there are either native, or well integrated."

"So... you might have more followers now. We invited those interested to visit us here at Murry Hill, they'll probably be here in a few days - we didn't want to pull anyone along by force. We should probably think of having someone here representing the interests of people beyond the Union's borders. With Tom here as well, it could become a workable embassy of sorts, I suppose. As long as Fuddles won't mind neighbors and we won't take too much of the park itself. Priorities are priorities. And you know, after this short trip, I think I have an idea what to do with all the leftover parts."

'Hey, Gil, you're likely already aware of at least some of this. But you know I've been looking for someone to keep an eye on the spiritual side of things here while we're away? I found someone I feel you'd approve of, an elf cleric named Ruto. He took refuge here with his friend Darunia, a tabaxi wildfire druid, a while ago. The two of them have been through some tough times even before the war started, they used to be pretty destructive, but they're trying their best to get their flames under control.'

'Darunia's not really religious, though Ruto told me that since they got here, he's been taking to thanking the souls of meat and fish he eats for the meal - Ruto, though, has been spiritual his whole life, although has been growing rather disillusioned lately due to worshipping a god of tempests. If he's willing, and you're willing, I would happily induct him as a cleric of peace under your guidance. Tonight, I'm going to take him to the pond, and fully explain the tenets, the meditation process, and the specifics of the role.'

"Evenin', Gil. Normally I would've done this as an end-of-day thing, but, well, we kinda got kept up in Feytown and ended up sleeping there. Sab says she felt kinda odd, but I didn't see much difference."

"Anyway, we went to chat with Ferrah and the shifter kids under her care. I wanted to ask them all about their plans, and suggested something for those undecided. You know how with my mostly being active at night and ending up doing support for those on the front line, and picking up some loose ends that needed doing, my values up from before just naturally aligned with your tenets? I was wondering if maybe the kids there would be interested in picking up some small errands that would help the city they live in. Especially that they're, well, they had to make a new family for themselves together. Give them the impression that they can make a difference, not just float wherever fate carries them."

"Darragh seems to be really on board, I think she'll be running things before we know it. As, well, my legacy of sorts, I suppose, I called this group of ours the Night Shifters. Yes, a few of them groaned, but I think it'll stick. Darragh's coming over later today, I promised her a tour of Murry Hill."

'Gil, Ruto's been doing great. I know that, you know that, you know I know that. But he's taken to the training like, ah...'
`A fish to water, you could say~`
'...yeah. I suppose you're not wrong. But Darunia tells me this is the happiest he's been since they were children. To have an actual way to change things... they were destructive because that's all they could do. But now, Ruto - the both of them, actually - have somewhere to contribute their energy, and it's really showing. They both get on well with the Night Shifters, too; they've taken on brotherly sort of roles, and Ruto especially is great at calming them down if there's a disagreement. Darunia's better at talking with adults, so he's helping out at the embassy, too.'
'Honestly, how well they work together, even when doing different things? Reminds me of Roy and myself. I'm certain that we made a good choice here.'

'Oh, yeah - you remember how, way back, Roy made the excuse of looking for a park location in order to check the Gazette cornerstone without telling us about it? Well, we've been thinking back on that, and... it would be a good place for a park, really. We'll have to get approval from the city, but I doubt they'd have a problem with it. If they allow us naming rights I'm going to suggest Liberty Park, I think it fits.'

`What's up, Gildmaster Sandytuff? Sab asked me to report in for her, she's meeting with borough officials. They want it made clear that the park will still be part of Hampstead rather than us building there making it a part of the Wilds, which - she's been telling them all along that yes, she has no intention of claiming the land, her only motivation is improving the borough's welfare for everyone who lives or visits there, no catch, but I guess with all the politics it needs to drag on longer. But you'd think they'd understand her intent with, I don't know, all the help we gave to the rest of rebuilding...`

"Hey, Gil. How are you doing? I hope we didn't keep you waiting for too long. We'll be departing the city soon. I think it's all progressing well and in good hands. I finished that thing I mentioned before. I'm calling it the Blue Strider. It'll help us travel, and be a home away from home. Well... A shelter, rather. I want to think of the wilds of Arcania as a home to care for wherever, so we would never really be away from home."

"I've been talking with folks from Feytown, to make the vehicle be like their wooden ferries and not make a mess wherever we'd go. It's not the fastest, but it's just the way I wanted. You know, having caring for nature be one of your tenets definitely made me change how I think of machines. Not like I was wasteful beforehand, just neutral, I suppose. But there's great value in enforcing our creations fitting with the environment around us."

"Anyway, the Strider will house me, Sab, Ed, Irynx, and Lilly, and should have room to spare should anyone else join us. I mean, aside from Grimmy. No force can contain Grimmy. Don't worry, it's not gonna stop us from actually getting out into nature. There's a lot to see for us, but... Well, I'm not able to say how I know it. In a week or two, when we have this chat, it won't be in Murry Hill for a while. But, all of rivers and lakes are under your care, right? I'm sure we'll find a place."

'Gil, as you can probably tell - I'm talking to you from the pond I made in Liberty Park.'
`It's in the shape of your face!`
'...no, it's not. I feel like carving nature into the shape of someone's face is... somewhat weird. And even if I was going to do that - they were already worried I had ulterior motives for requesting a pond in the first place. Which... yes, having a pond here is useful for us, but my main reasoning was, well - our people and others' hydration needs, as well as a place for animals to drink from.'
`So they put it up to a vote. I'm still mad the pigeon-shaped pond didn't win.`
'It ended up, hmm... sort of a lumpy horseshoe shape, with a large tree in the center. I like it, honestly. I've put a spectrum of flowers around it, and Roy's set up some glyphs to refill it if it runs empty. The cornerstone's surrounded by flowers, too, and there's talks of turning the old Gazette building into a museum...'

** **

`Oh, heya, Gil. Uh, it's me. Sorry if you expected Sab, she's not feeling too great. I kept telling her she's overworking herself... if any of us should overwork, it's me, an hour of ritual and a bundle of incense and I'm back no problem. But it's nothing major, at least, she just needs some rest. I'd be able to tell if it were serious, and yeah, I feel a little odd, but no sense of impending doom or existential despair today---hold on, she just woke up, I'll voice for her for a few. Just like old times, huh?`

'Gil, good morning... evening... whichever time it is. Don't worry about me, I've just been feeling a bit tired. Been making sure everything's ready for the trip tomorrow. It's odd how many things living people need to travel, compared to how little I came here with... Roy says hello, by the way. He's been looking after me, hasn't left my side since I, ah, slightly collapsed. Just a little bit, I'm alright. Everyone's enforcing rest on me... I guess I can see why, but it's a little frustrating. Ah - Ed's brought me soup, I'll talk to you later.'

`So yeah. Dunno what I'm feeling from her, feels a bit different to straight-up overwork, so I'm guessing anticipation's bleeding through with it. Which, I get it. I got put on moral support duty - we'll see how long that one lasts with all the puns I've been thinking up, hah - but I'm just so hyped for whatever we'll end up finding. Really strange feeling, that, like - I entered this city as Sab's Guide, now I'm guiding countless people to your shining light. Or something like that. Iunno. We all grew so much, huh?...anyway, gonna grab me some of that soup. You won't catch me missing out on Ed's cooking if I can help it. See ya later, Gill-pickle.`

'Gil... we're about to leave, so I have to be quick. Despite everything, I still feel burdened by the past. I need a decisive, final way to lift this weight... though, maybe... Yes, I think that will work. Thanks.'

Roy leads Sabrine to the Noir, somewhere reminiscent of their first expedition there.
"So, what are you leaving?"
*'My old cloak...* Sab says. *I'm not sure I ever mentioned it, but it was originally the shroud I was wrapped in for burial. It's been a shield for me for so long, since my second chance at life... But I don't need it any more. I'm hoping it can help others in the future, if I leave it here - help them to seize the day, live without regrets, and move forwards. Like I have.'*
Roy nods. "Yeah, that sounds like it might do some good here for someone."
*'How about you?'* She asks.
Roy shakes his head. "Well... I don't think I'm as profound. I was thinking the short bow you painted when I needed one, and the overalls I've had ever since before coming to Arcania. I mended and cleaned them, before you ask."
Looking a little surprised for a second, she nods. *'Yeah... That makes sense. It's not like you need it any more...'* a couple of tears come to her eyes. *'I'm glad it helped while it could.'*

"I didn't shoot it much before making Mended Anew," Roy starts. "But it wasn't the point. It was probably the first time since coming to Arcania that I actually felt useful, like I could do something. Perhaps someone else could use that feeling too. And the overalls, well, gotta be crafty, I suppose. And they've been home to my swarm for years. I guess you can find some deeper meaning here. Deeper than all the pockets sewn onto those."
The tears fall as Sabrine listens. *'I hope so. Sounds like all these should embody supporting oneself and others... That's concepts we could always use more of.'* before she laughs slightly, *'So if I made the bow and you put it here, does the resulting being count as our child?'*
"Uh..." Roy pauses. "Maybe? Ask the Noir, I don't know how it works." Roy neatly folds the overalls and puts them on a bench, and then puts the shortbow on the same bench at the other end. "I hope that'll work."

'It should? I'm not sure how long it takes, though... I might not live to see the results. Well, so long as it helps people out, I don't mind.'
*"Same."* Roy adds. *"I suppose you wanted to say something before leaving the cloak?"*
'Yes, though... not quite about it.' She takes a deep breath, kneels and continues to speak:

'Katrine. I'm moving on, for both our sakes. I know you wouldn't want me to be tied down by the past. My reminder...'
She pulls out her revolver, newly cleaned and polished; the name **Katrine's Sorrow** gone, neatly replaced with **Katrine's Requiem**.
'I placed this on myself as a burden, to prevent me from forgetting, though it caused me many problems. With this name change, I free myself of this burden, keeping only the memory.'
The gun is returned to its holster.
'Katrine, I may not remember your real name, what you look like, or any real details - but I remember you, and I always will. If you can hear me... I love you, sis.'
As she finishes speaking, she gently releases the shroud, letting it float where it will as the Noir takes it, eyes sparkling with both tears and the determination to move forwards.
Roy puts his hand on Sabrine's shoulder. *"Perhaps we'll meet whoever the cloak gives life to. Or we won't. We'll see. Anyway, shall we head back to the Strider? I suppose it's time to go."*
Sabrine nods and stands back up, taking his hand. 'It is, or so Kukudh says. Let's go.'
As they head back, her walk is somewhat wobbly, both from emotion and tiredness, but there's clearly a burden lifted from her mind and heart.

When the war ends, life continues. There's a lot that needs rebuilding, and so as much as Irynx would like to leave on the grand adventure she's been planning, she stays. She prepares, she ponders, she lives. 

First, she rechristens the Ball-Eater as the Raven Queen. It's a Raven class airship, she's a priestess of the Ravens; as much whimsy that decision took, it felt only right. 

The next and most immediate concern is rounding up all the animals who escaped from the zoo. It takes forever, unsurprisingly. For the rest of her time in Empire City, she walks across the street and sometimes runs into a lost caribou. 

She spends some of her time taking care of the grove and hanging out with Mim. Once, she takes Mim out for a night at Boompaleis with a few others. The goliath Torax, for some reason, is one of them. It is an experience the likes of which they are contractually obligated never to share. 

She helps rebuild the Ordinary and the rest of Hampstead, always offering help where she can, even if just to bring sandwiches for the people actually doing the work. Then again, the regular appearances of a giant ape definitely helped with the rebuilding efforts. Along with her friends in the night shift, they design the new Liberty Park around where the Empire Gazette stood.

After learning of Bo's departure from Ed, Irynx takes responsibility for the deal they made with Pinkerton all those months ago, and leaves a bottle of whiskey for the tiefling every two weeks. Whether she can keep this up once she leaves the city, she's unsure.
** **

And she makes her third and (hopefully) final deal with the ravens. Irynx Berlio walks out of Kingsbridge that day with a little bundle of a girl: Corbianne Berlio Lundsdóttir, the daughter of the grove. Knowing they'd leave one day, Irynx hopes that Cor will treasure these memories of Empire City when she grows up, of running around Murry Hill with Kukudh and Orphy, climbing the roots of Cael'fii, and helping count all the ball bearings in the Ordinary. 

The day comes when the work is done, and there's nothing left to do in Empire City. Irynx finds there are some things she'd like to leave behind after all. She leaves the Raven Queen to the Speaker for the Dead, and hopes it will become a home for him rather than just a warship. 

She packs more supplies than necessary for the journey, Irynx believes in being prepared. They have a going-away party, because of course they have to have a going away party, and then it's time for goodbye. Her daughter in one arm, and the mothman egg in another, her tale in Empire City ends. 

So begins <#880280609170264084>.

As the years began to blur by, Bo begins to lose all sense of time. He has no idea how many years he has been ferrying the dead, but one day... 

Lucy beams with excitement... 

Another Bo has seen before is about to ride, Lucy tells him. He ponders a moment, trying to guess who it could be before he shrugs and grabs his banjo, ready to ease the travel for whomever is joining him. The light grows brightly from lucy as she takes her post on the carpet, she begins giggling. 

A bright flash of light herolds the way... But... Something is off...

 Something, Bo hasnt quite fully expected. He is joined by two souls this time..."uh... This is new...." Another light beams from above..."t-three? All at once?!?!" As the light fades, the three souls sit formless in front of him, much like wisps.

Bo sits, blinking curiously. "Um... Uh... Hiya you three... " bo smiles warmly as he haphazardly waves, still confused. "Now then... Lets see your story shall we?" He asks as he bows graciously. As lucy flies around... She tilts her head as, something off-sets her. 

Before bo could start his normal ritual of playing his mother's lullaby... A song begins to echo from 2 of the 3 wisps. Lucy quickly moves in, and boops one of the wisps. Bo looks on, confused as the wisp takes form, and his ears twitch to the melody the goblin before him is singing. As Lucy boops the next wisp, the remaining 2 wisps take form. A Goblin in armor, and a small puppy... The song becomes shockingky clear to Bo now. The two goblins before him... Are singing his mother's lullaby. He quickly adds to the melody andnsings along, much to the suprise of Rockman and Leaf. It takes a moment for bo to recognize one of the goblins, before he begins to be licked by a small puppy. It is indeed a very small dog, but his bark echoes through the realm Bo travels in.

Bo pets the puppy only briefly, before a memory flashes in his head, the oasis. "HEY! ..... Ain't you... Gil's friend?" Bo asks. The male goblin gives bo a thumbs up and smiles.
"Yeap! You were there in Gil's oasis the day he appeared, weren't ya?" Lucy beams in, and in an instant, he witnesses the life story of the 3... Of Rockman, Leaf, and Rush. 

Bo's eyes grow wide with excitement as he see's Sandigil, the coins passed around for his mayoral candidacy. He's excited to watch....up until bo himself see's the horrors in town square, Sandigil's head on a pike. The fight with the Hunger... And the wish rockman had made... To wish Sandigil back to life. He quickly moves over and shakes Rickman's hand, as Leaf steps forward and asks how it was that Bo knew their song. 

Dormant memories flood Bo's mind, of being a smol bun. He had scrapped his knee... And his mother begain singing. 
"Mama, where'd you learn that song?" Bo asked.
All she responded with, was a smile as he kept singing.

"My mother sang it to me... Later on she finally told me, that lullaby had been passed down for generations." Bo chuckkes. Rockman and Leaf both look towards each other and smile, holding hands.

Meanwhile, the puppy Rush flies around chasing a panicking Lucy. Voices echo from the two as they spin around in the air.
"play? Play? Play?" -rush
"Aaaaaah he's so slobery!" -lucy

Bo, Rockman, and Leaf all laugh together as the carpet, at first unknowingly to Bo, slowly rises up. Higher and higher as a light beams down from the sky above.

As they sit and talk, Bo eventually notices the change in scenery. As golden light fills the area, a small fish flies down, spinning around Leaf. Leaf's face beams with joy as Rush and Lucy fly over. The trio ascend up even higher as Rockman and Leaf begins to phase back into living boddies. Bo looks on in amazement as the puppy grows and his bark begins to deepen. 

"Mello!" Rockman and Leaf both cheer in ecitement as they both move in to hug the fish. In another flash, the fish transformed into that of a young woman. Bo smiles and sits back, letting the three float up. 

Bo exchanges waves with the trio as they fade away with Mello. As the carpet descends back to the River, bo smiles. Lucy beams down and nuzzles bo before they resume their journey along the river.

On the banks near by, a form fades as they smile up to the sky. Web sighs as their voice echoes.

"Truly goodbye this time. Take good care, Mello. Take good care." -Web.

So this is not an IC epilogue, but more of my way of thanking you all as my way of wrapping up the season.  I won’t speak for other DMs, but my journey this season really did start last season.  Thank you all for letting me say goodbye to my favorite character.  And thank you all for saying goodbye.  He’s now part of the official lore of Arcania, but in my mind Gil’s story is over.  He will appear in the future, but only as the other wardens do, both a part of the world, and not a part of the game, touching where they need to, but not super active presence.

I set out this season to give anyone who needs it closure with him, but in the end, I got the closure I needed.  So again, thank you for that.

Beyond that, I got to write so much content for the creepy oppressive section of town.  I was so excited to see Crane breathe life into it, and other DMs take time to run things there.  It was a blast to see you all deal with the horrors that were in every nook and cranny of Hampstead.  Every time you all had an event there, I had trouble sleeping, so excited to find out the next day how it went.  And man, you all went above and beyond what I could have hoped.  So again, thank you.  I don’t think I would have made it through the season without the players seeming so encouraged by the content I wrote.

We all went through a lot this season, just as we did last season, but most importantly, we have all expanded the community, and created new friendships.  Anyway, I want to thank you all for giving life to the world we built.  Without the players, there really would be no game, and no reason for the DMs to plan.  I’ll see you all on the Tales server, I am sure.  It’ll go quiet from time to time, but know, we will be working on S5, with the same love and care we gave S4.

Love,
Heki AKA Sandigil

The Epilogue of a Certain Café

**Eliot:** 
After spending a bit further time with Jigsaw, Raxacoricofallapatorius, and Mike, Eloise excuses herself to return to the Crepes and Crits Café, meeting with Willow outside to have another heavy conversation along with collecting some personal belongings,  Before returning to Cael'fii and Demetrius.

With the king dead, the war over, and the city and nation uniting, things seem to be settling down, as settle as a major metropolis can be under such conditions. Eloise takes a few hours each day to begin teaching Sabrine Arcanian Sign Language, (at no cost) which Roy and Kukudh are welcome to participate in. She aids in rebuilding the park in New Hempstead using a few uses of Plant Growth. 

As everything settles down and Eloise has more time to sort out her thoughts and feelings she asks those closest to her to refer to them as El, and while they still didn't quite feel like themselves they felt better than before.

El says goodbye to the part of themselves that was Eloise one week after their death and rebirth. They are glad to have had the opportunity to form the happy memories they did and  come to peace with who they were once upon a time, but it is not who they are.

After informing Demetrius of where El was at, in regards to finding themselves, El begins to grow more secretive and recluse. Not out of any wrongdoing or deteriorating mental state, simply the impending deadline of the pact made. The deadline and responsibility weigh on El as if they were carrying the whole cafe and the foundation of which it stood upon their back. 

On September 6th, 1776 two days prior to the deadline El presents a masterful blend of tea to Demetrius, beaming with pride, glad to finally have kept their part of their deal. However, it was still lacking something and it was not enough to leave Demetrius speechless nor was it the perfect blend. Shattered, heartbroken and defeated, realizing that no matter how much effort they put in within the next two days it would not be enough. The months they had spent afraid of the outside finally taking its toll. Through tears El pledged their eternal service to Demetrius until they were able to get it right.

thread: The Epilogue of a Certain Café

content:
Shortly following this pledge, El put Willow in charge of the cafe until the debt was paid off. They donned their tailcoat and accompanied Demetrius most places, when allowed, and offered their services where applicable as a butler. Secretly El was happy to spend as much time as they could in Demetrius' company, and it was a secret not well hidden from the other court members of Feyrytown. But El kept their demeanor professional regardless of who Demetrius was meeting with and always had tea on hand. On the extraordinarily rare occurrence where meetings took a darker turn, El also performed the duties of a bodyguard. Not that the ancient fey needed the help, but as a way to help insure neither resorted to their violent pasts. 
Six months after their death, El returns to being Eliot, once more comfortable in who he is. Eliot dyes his hair back to his well known mint color, but there is a single streak of gold along the left side. Three years of companionship and servitude to Demetrius pass before they are granted passage, for a singular day, to where Demetrius' home once was. Upon seeing the beauty, Eliot understood what his tea had been missing. He separates himself from Demetrius for a short time to gather some flowers and a bit of the soil. Saving them for a later surprise.

On the anniversary of their fifth year together Eliot invites Demitrius on a surprise trip for their anniversary, Eliot is shy but proud to show Demetrius the Demiplane he had crafted for the couple to share, a replica of Demetrius’ home. It wasn’t quite perfect, but it was enough for the two of them to call their own home.

thread: The Epilogue of a Certain Café

content:
Years pass, and Eliot grows older yet Demitrius remains the same. Eliot has a longing to be part of Demitrius’ life for as long as the fey had already lived. But knows he can’t, instead he looks into something originally only a fleeting desire from his youth, and came back to him briefly in the presence of a certain radiant familiar. Eliot looks into dragons and their kin. A child the couple could raise together, and not be bound by Eliot’s own mortality. He didn’t want Demetris to grieve his passing, or worsen it by a child of theirs also passing long before the archfey’s time was up.

It took several more years before Eliot was able to get an egg with help from Prosser stopping some smugglers. Then presenting it to Demetrius, a large egg coated in deep red scales. Despite the off color Eliot consider’s Trapero as a name for the dragon, but discusses it with Prosser first. They mention that if it were to be named in Trapero’s honor they’d prefer it to be Prospero, the name the twins held before they were split.  

Soon after receiving the egg the small red dragon is running amok and driving Eliot up walls just to keep up with the wild child and its flames. Despite all the stress a smile never leaves his face, particularly when seeing young Prospero and Demetrius bonding while Eliot cleans scorch marks and regrows flowers.

Many uneventful years pass, and Eliot enjoys the chaotic peace with his small family. But he knows his life is drawing near. Many other humans he’s known of his years have passed, and he’s seen waves upon wave’s of Sutri’s own children become adults in their own right, and even see some of them move on to whatever happened next. He takes Demetrius out one one more date, to the small little cafe that began it all, and brews up a pot of tea for them both. A special recipe he had figured out oh so many years ago, on the trip to Demitrius’ home. A recipe he didn’t need to be confident in, a recipe he knew was the one. He sat across from Demitrius and acted as if there was nothing special about the tea by taking the first sip, before relishing the look on his partner’s face and making a gentle comment that he finally paid of his debt for fulfilling his childhood dream, and being thankful to have helped make so many other people’s dreams come true, including his own, all at the side of the most wonderful partner.

content: Eliot passes away in his sleep two weeks later on August 24, 1846. Exactly seventy years after The Whispering Wolf killed him, at the age of 97. Leaving behind Demetrius, their 53 year old child, and the cafe. His will does not contain much, as he never had much. He does leave behind a very precious tea pot, inside on a very worn and folded piece of paper is the recipe for the perfect tea, which he leaves to Demetrius. And the intricate silver timepiece he leaves for Prospero as a memento.

**Willow:**
Willow learned Eliot's lessons with a great interest and took his plans for the café and built upon it. She continued to run the café, although the hours fluctuated for a time as there was no longer a manager that didn't sleep, many of the regular cliental understood however and gave the café the opportunity it needed to grow from where Eliot had started. Willow allowed stray animals to continue to come, go and  volunteer, however she was noticeably more determined to have a working staff over volunteers to provide a better service to the customers of the café. 

True to her words with Demetrius and Ferrah, she helped couch other animals through the process and eventual awakening of those under her employ. Not all took her up on the offer which she understood, it was a lot to process and even a few years after her own awakening found it a lot to deal with and missed simpler times.

On multiple occasions, larger businesses attempted to buy out the café, only to have their attempts thwarted and offers returned in shreds. Leaving them to settle for cheap knock offs of the critter exclusively operated café, such as Starpaws or Cheesy Chucks, which were only humanoids in animal costume.

One side effect that she had *not* been prepared for due to her Awakening was an extended life span compared to what she would have normally expected.  She owned and operated the cafe the remainder of her days. Willow passes on in her sleep June 23, 1821 at the age of 53.
